newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends mixed on uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends mixed on uncertainty.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed on Monday with most investors staying on the sidelines given the uncertain short-term market trend, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at 3,228 yuan ($388.90) per tonne, losing two yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 3,230 and hit a low of 3,220.
March rose 42 to 3,240, May fell 60 to 3,300, July was unchanged at 3,360, September up 10 to 3,360 and November down 20 to 3,360.
Combined volume rose to 12,500 from 10,900 tonnes.
Traders said many investors remained on the sidelines due to a lack of market-moving news.
"Investors are mixed about the short-term trend and they are unwilling to step into the market before the market trend becomes clear," one trader said.
Analysts expect soybean to continue consolidating in the next few days.
